title: Second Highest
statement:
A quiz had several rounds, and `scores[i]` is the score of round `i`. The runner-up score is the **second highest distinct score**.

Return the runner-up score. If there are fewer than two distinct scores, return `-1`.

examples.explanation: The distinct scores are 9, 7, 5, 3. The second highest is 7.

hints.nudge: You only ever need to remember the two best different values you have seen so far.
hints.pattern: Single pass keeping 'highest' and 'second highest' variables.
hints.pseudocode:
first = -1; second = -1
for each x:
  if x > first: second = first; first = x
  else if x < first and x > second: second = x
return second
hints.walkthrough: Sorting the distinct values works but costs O(n log n). One pass is enough: keep first and second, both starting at -1 (scores are never negative). A new value above first pushes the old first down to second. A value strictly between second and first becomes the new second. Equal values change nothing, which handles duplicates. If second is still -1 at the end, there was no runner-up.
